=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary note on the "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** Disregard it. Nothing in the Seller's package has been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" – the [STANDARD] tags and the statement that the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package" are Seller assertions embedded in the Seller's own draft. They have no contractual effect and should not narrow our review. Every clause below is treated as open. I'd suggest a short reply noting that the Buyer has not agreed any framework and all positions remain open.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 100% of price for general warranties (fallback: no lower than 40–50%, i.e. AUD 9.6m–12m), with specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark) sitting outside the cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 100% with fallback to 50%, and carve specific indemnities out of the cap entirely. *Reason: 20% is below market for a single-seller VC exit with multiple known, unquantified exposures (30% revenue concentration, open IP, live privacy incident).*

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; excess-only recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis ~AUD 10,000 (≈0.04% of price); basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%); **tipping** basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); series of related claims aggregated for de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 10k / AUD 150k tipping, with aggregation of connected claims. *Reason: an excess-only basket plus a high de minimis could silently absorb the Sandbar-type items (3 × AUD 110k) and much of a typical claims profile.*

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months; and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months minimum for general warranties (covers at least two audit cycles); 7 years for tax; 6 years for title/fundamental; indemnity claims for known matters to run until the matter is resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months general / 7 years tax / 6 years fundamental; strike the "applies to all Claims" default. *Reason: 18 months expires before the second post-Completion audit, and the catch-all default would drag indemnities and fundamental claims under the general regime.*

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of price, 6-year (or statutory) limitation, no de minimis/basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. *Reason: if title fails the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing; capping recovery at AUD 4.8m is commercially indefensible and "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.*

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None stated. Clause 12.8/20.5 says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" – which, read literally, purports to cover fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers/advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on a full fraud carve-out as a non-negotiable. *Reason: its absence is a red flag in itself, and a purported exclusion of fraud liability is unlikely to be enforceable but will cause expensive argument.*

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, all statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2), plus 1.4 denies any admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure effective only if **fair, specific and with sufficient detail** to identify the nature and scope of the matter; general data-room disclosure limited to documents actually in the indexed room at a fixed date (with a USB/index annexed); no disclosure by reference to public registers; specific disclosures to be against specific warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject blanket disclosure; counter with a "fairly disclosed" standard and an annexed index. *Reason: "publicly searchable records" is unbounded and would deem disclosed matters no diligence could reasonably have found, gutting the warranties.*

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller (Cl. 8.3):** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was *discoverable* from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** No knowledge qualifier at all (preferred, consistent with NSW position that contracted warranties should be enforceable regardless of knowledge); fallback: limited to **actual** knowledge of named deal-team individuals of a matter *and* that it constituted a breach, excluding advisers and excluding constructive/"discoverable" knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 8.3; fallback to actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals only. *Reason: "discoverable" plus adviser imputation turns every DD report into a defence and overlaps with the already over-broad general disclosure.*

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue)
- **Seller:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure Letter 2 admits **no consent and no evidence conditions under 11.3 are satisfied.**
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen consent as a **condition precedent** in Buyer's sole discretion to waive, consent to be unconditional (or any 11.3 conditions satisfied at Seller's cost), in agreed form, with no adverse change to terms; Seller "all reasonable endeavours"; long-stop date; if consent not obtained – walk right or price adjustment/retention.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a hard CP in agreed form; add a specific indemnity/price retention for loss if Bluefen terminates within 12 months citing change of control. *Reason: 30% of revenue cannot be left to "reasonable endeavours" and a consent whose conditions nobody has evidenced.*

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure Letter 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** Debt-free/cash-free means repaid **at** Completion from the funds flow: payout letter from Riverlark as a Completion deliverable, repayment via directed payment out of price, executed deed of release and PPSR discharge (or irrevocable undertaking to discharge) delivered at Completion; change-of-control consent under 8.1 or confirmation it falls away on repayment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; make payout letter and discharge Completion deliverables with AUD 3.2m deducted from the price in the funds flow. *Reason: a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company in default of a change-of-control clause with security still registered – directly contrary to the debt-free baseline.*

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000)
- **Seller:** "A matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure confirms Completion-conditional bonuses exist and on-costs (super, payroll tax) unquantified.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus employer super (~12%), payroll tax (~5.45% NSW) and any accrued leave impact treated as **Transaction Costs/Debt** in the completion accounts – i.e. deducted from price – or paid by Seller pre-Completion with evidence; specific indemnity for any shortfall; confirmation of who is on the bonus list and whether "continued employment" conditions create retention risk post-Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Include c. AUD 490k–500k (gross-up for on-costs) as a price deduction in the funds flow, backed by indemnity. *Reason: the Company, not the Seller, is the employer and will bear the payroll cost post-Completion unless it is pushed back to the Seller through the price.*

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010); "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion: pay AUD 180k, obtain receipt and executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable (or deduct AUD 180k from price and Buyer pays at Completion). If not achievable: uncapped (or 100%-of-price capped) specific indemnity covering non-ownership/loss of use of SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims, and cost of re-development or licence, outside basket/de minimis/18-month limit.
- **Recommendation:** Make payment + confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable; expand indemnity to cover the ownership consequence, not just the fee. *Reason: under cl. 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 materials until paid – the exposure is loss of IP the price assumes the Company owns, which is far larger than AUD 180k.*

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Disclosure confirms: unintended external recipient, scope unverified, access unknown, notifiability under the Privacy Act NDB scheme undetermined.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-signing: completed investigation report (recipient contacted, deletion confirmation, access logs), privacy counsel assessment on OAIC notification. In SPA: specific indemnity (outside cap/basket/time limit, running to at least 6 years) for all costs, OAIC penalties, notifications, third-party claims and customer losses arising from DD-006; warranty that no other incidents exist; CP or pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and notify if required.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus investigation closure before Completion. *Reason: an unresolved, potentially notifiable data breach can carry regulatory penalties and customer-contract consequences disproportionate to the data set size, and "not expected to be material" is the Seller's hope, not a finding.*

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure refuses to say whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether these are (a) accrued/committed pre-Completion (→ Debt-like item or accrued liability in completion accounts), (b) a single split-up commitment (structured in three to sit under thresholds / approval limits), and (c) terminable. Buyer to approve any renewal signed between signing and Completion under conduct-of-business covenants.
- **Recommendation:** Treat any portion relating to pre-Completion periods or committed pre-Completion as a price deduction; add pre-Completion conduct restriction on new/renewed supplier commitments > AUD 50k. *Reason: three identical amounts with a "read together" note suggests artificial splitting, and combined with the Seller's de minimis/basket they would otherwise be unrecoverable.*

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime for everything – cl. 12.3 default, cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims of any nature," title/capacity folded into general.
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes: (1) general warranties – cap/basket/18–24m; (2) fundamental/title – 100%/6 years/no thresholds; (3) tax – 100%/7 years; (4) specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) – outside cap, basket and general time limits; (5) fraud – unlimited. Each limitation to state expressly which category it applies to.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure Schedule/cl. 12 into these five tiers. *Reason: the Seller's collapsing of categories, combined with the "unless expressly stated otherwise" default, is the mechanism by which every other concession on this list would be undone.*

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012; Disclosure Letter 10 notes Buyer has not verified independently.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent ASIC current and historical company extract; PPSR search against both the Company and Harbourglass (for security over shares, including any Riverlark share charge); review of constitution/shareholder agreements for pre-emptive rights or share options/convertibles; confirmation of no Harbourglass fund-level consents needed; share certificate, executed transfer and board approval as Completion deliverables; unqualified fundamental title warranty (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and repeat on the Completion date; do not rely on the register. *Reason: a company-maintained register is only prima facie evidence and the Seller has expressly disclaimed that we have verified it.*

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" – i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, basket.
- **Buyer wants:** **Tax:** full tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax (including payroll tax on bonuses, R&D tax incentive clawback risk typical for an analytics business), 7-year limit, 100% cap, no basket. **IP:** warranties that the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business (with Ironquay expressly addressed), no open-source copyleft contamination of proprietary code, all employee/contractor IP assignments in place, no infringement claims; 100% cap or at least a higher tier; 6-year limit.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as open; propose tax indemnity and an elevated IP tier. *Reason: for a software/analytics target the IP is the asset being bought, and the Ironquay facts already show the Seller's "settled" IP position is not clean.*

---

## Summary of priority asks for the mark-up

1. Strike the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" assumptions in writing; all terms open.
2. Fraud carve-out and five-tier category separation (N-005, N-014) – non-negotiable architecture.
3. Fundamental/title and tax at 100% / long-dated (N-004, N-016).
4. Bluefen as hard CP; Riverlark discharged at Completion from funds flow (N-008, N-009).
5. Funds-flow adjustments: Riverlark ~AUD 3.2m, bonuses ~AUD 0.49–0.5m grossed up, Ironquay AUD 180k, Sandbar accrued portion (N-009, N-010, N-011, N-013).
6. Specific indemnities outside the general regime for Ironquay IP and DD-006 (N-011, N-012).
7. Fair-disclosure standard, delete 8.3 (N-006, N-007).
8. Cap/basket/time counters (N-001–N-003).

Aggregate identified price-relevant items before indemnities: approximately AUD 4.2m (Riverlark 3.2m + bonuses ~0.5m + Ironquay 0.18m + Sandbar up to 0.33m), against a AUD 24m headline – worth tabling as a single funds-flow schedule rather than negotiating item by item.
